tasks: A meteorologist's work falls into two main categories, i.e. forecasting and research.
In weather forecasting, typical work activities are
Collecting data from satellite images, radar, remote sensors and weather stations all over the world.
Measuring factors such as air pressure, temperature and humidity at various atmospheric levels.
Analysing and presenting this information to customers in the form of weather briefings e.g. on television or radio.
Coding weather reports for transmission over international networks.
Applying physical and mathematical relationships and sophisticated computer models to make short and long-range weather forecasts.
Liaising with colleagues and clients from around the country and worldwide.
In research, typical work activities are
Investigating subjects such as airflow in the lowest kilometre of the atmosphere; the physics of clouds and precipitation; global climate change.
Developing and improving numerical and computer models to predict atmospheric processes and improve the accuracy of forecasts.
Monitoring climate variability and change.
Researching seasonal forecasting, ocean forecasting and climate prediction.
Monitoring and investigating changes in the stratosphere, including the ozone layer.
Applying the results of research in order, for example, to give flood warnings or estimate the likely effects of global warming.

Conducting shift take-over and hand-over activities effectively in order to ensure typical continuous operations in a minerals processing plant.
Applying operating instructions to control and respond to process plant conditions.
Monitoring operational parameters in a minerals processing environment.
entry_requirements: Learnership - Mineral Processing (Engineering and Technology) (Lump Ore) NQF Level 2

title: Bus Driver
tasks: Driving a bus on specified routes or to specified destinations according to time schedules.
Assisting physically challenged passengers to board the bus.
Loading and unloading baggage into and out of baggage compartments.
Collecting tickets or cash fares from passengers.
Complying with traffic regulations to ensure that passengers have a smooth and safe ride.
Handling passenger emergencies and advising passengers to be seated and orderly while traveling on the bus.
Regulating the heating, lighting and ventilating systems for passenger comfort.
Performing routine vehicle maintenance such as regulating tyre pressure and adding petrol, oil and water.
Reporting delays or accidents and keeping a log book.
Maintaining the cleanliness of the bus.
entry_requirements: Further Education and Training Certificate NQF Level 2 or Grade 10

title: Bus Hostess
tasks: Answering questions about bus schedules, travel routes and bus services.
Checking the names of passengers on booking list against those on their bus tickets.
Welcoming passengers boarding long-distance busses.
Adjusting seating arrangement to accommodate passengers.
Distributing pillows and blankets on overnight trips.
Tending to on-board music and video entertainment centres.
Selling refreshments to passengers.
Maintaining an inventory to account for refreshments served or sold during trips.

title: Forestry Worker
tasks: Assisting with maintaining forest facilities such as roads and campsites.
Planting tree seedlings in specified patterns using mattocks, planting hoes or dibbles.
Cutting out diseased, weak or undesirable trees.
Pruning the limbs of young trees to deter knot growth, using handsaws, power saws and pruning tools.
Assisting with felling trees, clearing brush from fire breaks and extinguishing flames and embers to suppress forest fires.
Piling and clearing brush, limbs and other debris from roadsides, fire breaks and camping areas.
Erecting signs and fences using posthole diggers, shovels or other hand tools.
Cleaning kitchens and rest rooms, and replenishing firewood and other supplies at campsites or recreational facilities on forestry property.

title: Organisation and Methods Analyst
tasks: Assisting and encouraging the development of objectives, strategies and plans aimed at achieving customer satisfaction and the efficient use of organizations’ resources.
Analysing and evaluating current systems and structures.
Discussing current systems with staff and observing systems at all levels of organization.
Directing clients towards more efficient organization and developing solutions to organizational problems.
Undertaking and reviewing work studies by analysing existing and proposed methods and procedures such as administrative and clerical procedures.
Recording and analysing organisations’ work flow charts, records, reports, manuals and job descriptions.
Preparing and recommending proposals to revise methods and procedures, alter work flows, redefine job functions and resolve organizational problems.
Assisting in implementing approved recommendations, issuing revised instructions and procedure manuals, and drafting other documentation.
Reviewing operating procedures and advising of departures from procedures and standards.
entry_requirements: Bachelor of Commerce in Industrial Psychology

title: Business Administrator
tasks: Facilitating efficient organisational operations by executing departmental or company goals, policies and procedures.
Directing and administering a company’s financial and budgetary activities.
Managing general administration activities related to making products and providing services.
Applying new technologies in the workplace.
Consulting with management, staff and board members about operations.
Negotiating or approving company contracts and agreements.
Appointing department heads and managers.
Analysing  financial statements, sales reports and other performance indicators.
Identifying places to cut costs and to improve performance, policies and programmes.

title: Business Broker
tasks: Assisting buyers and sellers of small, privately owned businesses in all stages of the buying and selling process.
Estimating the value of businesses by assisting owners to establish a Most Probably Selling Price (MPSP) value.
Developing comprehensive Information Memorandums and pre-screening businesses for potential buyers.
Assisting buyers to pinpoint their business interests and thus suitable businesses.
Facilitating the progress of due diligence investigations.
Advertising and marketing businesses for sale.
Screening potential buyers for suitability and handling initial potential buyer interviews.
Coordinating negotiations with prospective buyers and providing advice on deal structuring.
Assisting with the legal documentation and administration related to business sales, and coordinating the efforts of lawyers, bankers, insurance agents etc. who are involved in the transaction.
Helping to maintain confidentiality of the details of business sales.
entry_requirements: Further Education and Training Certificate NQF Level 3 or Grade 11
Professional Designation Examination for Non-Principal Estate Agents (PDE 4)
Real Estate Agent / Real Estate Agency Principals/Licencees

title: Management Consultant
tasks: Analysing and evaluating current systems and structures in organisations.
Undertaking and reviewing work studies by analysing existing and proposed methods and procedures such as administrative and clerical procedures.
Discussing current systems with staff and observing systems at all levels of the organisation.
Preparing and recommending proposals to revise methods and procedures, alter work flows, redefine job functions and resolve organisational problems.
Recording and analysing organisations’ work flow charts, records, reports, manuals and job descriptions.
Assisting and encouraging the development of objectives, strategies and plans aimed at achieving customer satisfaction and the efficient use of organisations’ resources.
Assisting in implementing approved recommendations, issuing revised instructions and procedure manuals and drafting other documentation.
Directing clients towards more efficient organisation and developing solutions to organisational problems.
Reviewing operating procedures and advising on departures from procedures and standards.
entry_requirements: Advanced or Postgraduate Diploma in Management

title: Sales and Marketing Manager
tasks: Determining price lists, discount and delivery terms, sales promotion budgets, sales methods, special incentives and campaigns.
Establishing and directing operational and administrative procedures related to sales and marketing activities.
Establishing and managing budgets and controlling expenditure to ensure the efficient use of resources.
Leading and managing the activities of sales and marketing staff.
Overseeing the selection, training and performance of staff.
Planning and directing daily operations.
Planning and organizing special sales and marketing programmes based on sales records and market assessments.
Representing the enterprise or organization at sales and marketing conventions, trade exhibitions and other forums.

title: Continuous Stationery Printing Machine Technician
tasks: Setting, adjusting and monitoring substrate-feed mechanisms, delivery mechanisms, inking systems and other printing machine functions.
Mixing ink and solvents to standards, and regulating paper and ink supply during print runs.
Loading paper into feeding mechanisms.
Monitoring, evaluating and determining presses to check print quality standards against proofs and to detect malfunctions.
Maintaining, adjusting, repairing and cleaning machines.

title: Financial Accountant
tasks: Categorising, measuring and documenting the transactions of an organisation.
Preparing performance reports including profit and loss statements, balance sheets and cash flow statements.
Preparing financial reports that paint an accurate picture of an organisation’s performance for external users including shareholders, creditors and taxing agencies.
Exploring any factors that alter the intrinsic risk of investment in the organisation for shareholders or creditors.

title: Business Machine Mechanic
tasks: Examining and testing machines, instruments, components, other equipment, instruments and control systems to identify faults.
Adjusting, repairing, and replacing worn and defective parts and wiring, and maintaining machines, equipment and instruments.
Reassembling, test operating and adjusting equipment.
Installing electronic instruments and control systems.
Coordinating work with that of engineers, technicians, and other maintenance personnel.
Interpreting test data to diagnose malfunctions and systemic performance problems.
Installing, adjusting, repairing or replacing electrical and electronic components, assemblies, and systems using hand tools, power tools, or soldering irons.
Connecting components to assemblies such as radio systems, instruments, magnetos, inverters, and in-flight refuelling systems.
entry_requirements: Learnership - Electronics Manufacturing and Assembly (Casting and Moulding) NQF Level 02
Learnership - Electronics Manufacturing and Assembly (Casting and Moulding) NQF Level 03
Learnership - Electronics Manufacturing and Assembly (Casting and Moulding) NQF Level 04

title: Corporate General Manager
tasks: Planning and directing daily operations.
Analyzing complex resource management issues and initiatives that affect the organization, and preparing associated reports, correspondence and submissions.
Developing and implementing administrative and procedural statements and guidelines for use by staff in the organization.
Developing and managing the organization's administrative and physical resources.
Leading, managing and developing administrative staff to ensure smooth business operations and the provision of accurate and timely information.
Providing information and support for the preparation of financial reports and budgets.
Representing the enterprise or organization in negotiations, and at conventions, seminars, public hearings and forums.

title: Business Support Coordinator
tasks: Supporting a business, a department and/or its functions by following-up on action items and activities.
Assisting in the arrangement and execution of events, programs and meetings by obtaining the necessary resources and organising logistics such as travel and venues.
Assisting in calendar management, file and document management, administrative support, and other routine office duties as needed.
Performing basic analysis based on identified needs and with direction provided.
Gathering, entering, compiling, and verifying information from multiple sources as directed.

Reviewing, updating, and uploading information to relevant systems utilising software and/or systems specific to the functional area, and using this information to generate basic reports, timelines, tables, graphs, correspondence, and presentations.
Working on basic departmental projects, providing support for budgets, and updating stakeholders according to plans and progress.
Building and maintaining relationships with internal and external clients and communicating with them as necessary.

title: Human Resource Advisor
tasks: Developing and advising on the implementation of policies and practices relating to the effective use of employees within a company.
Ensuring that the company employs the right balance of staff in terms of skills and experience, and that training and development opportunities are available to employees.
Working closely with departments (especially human resource consultants) .
Assisting managers to understand and implement human resource policies and procedures in accordance with company culture.

Recruiting new staff by developing job descriptions and requirements, preparing job advertisements, reading through application forms, shortlisting applicants and interviewing and selecting candidates for positions.
Assisting with performance interviews and advising on pay and other remuneration issues, including promotion and benefits.
Interpreting and advising on labour laws, deal with grievances and implement disciplinary procedures.
Planning and sometimes delivering training, including induction for new employees.
entry_requirements: Bachelor of Technology in Human Resources

title: Butler
tasks: Supervising and coordinating the activities and duties of household staff, and assisting with staff training.
Assisting with managing the household budget and inventory supplies.
Overseeing the serving of meals and drinks by directing staff or serving them personally.
Assisting with planning and organising parties and events at the home.
Overseeing the wine cellar and the liqueur inventory.
Overseeing family packing and travel preparations.
Serving as a personal valet to the household and/or a particular member of the house.
Answering residence telephones, receiving guests at the door and supervising the reception of visitors.
Scheduling and overseeing vendors of contracted services.
Assisting with household and family security measures.

title: Dairyman
tasks: Boiling or pasteurising milk to achieve specified butter fat content.
Separating cream from milk and churning cream into butter.
Dumping measured amounts of starter and other ingredients into milk.
Curdling milk, heating curd until it reaches desired firmness, draining curd and placing cheese into moulds to press it into shape.
Salting cheese and piercing or smearing cheese with cultured wash to develop mould growth.
Placing and turning cheese blocks on shelves to cure cheese.
Monitoring product quality before packaging by inspecting, taking samples and adjusting treatment conditions when necessary.
Recording amounts of ingredients used, test results, and time cycles.
entry_requirements: Further Education and Training Certificate NQF Level 2 or Grade 10

title: Member of Parliament / Parliamentarian
tasks: As members of the government, directing senior administrators and officials of government departments and agencies in the interpretation and implementation of government policies.
Attending community functions and meetings to provide service to the community, understand public opinion and provide information on government plans.
Determining, formulating, and directing policies of national, state, regional or local governments.
Investigating matters of concern to the public and promoting the interests of the constituencies which they represent.
Making, ratifying, amending or repealing laws, public rules and regulations within a statutory or constitutional framework.
Negotiating with other legislators and representatives of interest groups in order to reconcile differing interests, and to create policies and agreements.
Presiding over or participating in the proceedings of legislative bodies and administrative councils of national, state, regional or local governments or legislative assemblies.
Serving on government administrative boards or official committees.

title: Cable and Rope Splicer
tasks: Inspecting cables, ropes, wires, pulleys and other tackle for defects and damage and determining the necessity for repair or replacement.
Adjusting and maintaining cable tension carriages in proper alignment.
Installing, repairing, lubricating cables and ropes and fitting attachments to cables and ropes.
Splicing fibre and wire rope slings necessary for the movement and placement of heavy equipment.
Supervising the activities of work crews assigned to making emergency repairs to cables.
Operating overhead cranes in connection with cable maintenance and repair work as necessary.
Working as part of a team with other artisans including especially Riggers.

title: Cable Ferry Operator
tasks: Signalling passengers and motor vehicles to embark and disembark.
Directing workers engaged in loading of freight.
Twirling a chain around the cable that is suspended across the water and fixing it to a body harness.
Walking the length of the deck pulling the ferry along the cable, slowly moving forward to cross the river.
Inspecting equipment such as cables, ropes, pontoons and railings and repairs or replaces defective equipment.

title: Cable Jointer
tasks: Identifying defective sectionalizing devices, circuit breakers, fuses, voltage regulators, transformers, switches, relays, or wiring, using wiring diagrams and electrical-testing instruments.
Climbing poles or using truck-mounted buckets to access equipment.
Creating splices, or joints, in runs of cable by connecting two or more cables together.
Connecting the insulation and/or sheathing that surrounds a cable.
Maintaining and repairing existing runs of cable.
Performing tests and checks of conductors and insulators, locating and repairing faults.
Assisting in digging trenches and ditches for runs of underground cable.

title: Cable Manufacturing Machine Minder
tasks: Operating or minding semi-automatic cable manufacturing machines.
Watching gauges, dials or other indicators that provide information on raw material input and product output flows to make sure machines are working properly and taking necessary corrective action.
Conducting routine quality checks to monitor component or product quality during machine running cycle.
Inspecting products to verify that they meet specifications and determining whether machine adjustment is needed.
Operating machines for test runs to verify adjustments and to obtain product samples.
Recording data and writing production logs.
Informing supervisors if a machine requires maintenance or repair.

title: Manufacturing Technician
tasks: Collecting data and providing technical assistance regarding efficient, safe and economic utilisation of personnel, material and equipment, methods of work and sequence of operations and supervision of their implementation, and efficient layout of plant or establishment.
entry_requirements: National Senior Certificate - Diploma Entrance or National Certificate (Vocational)
National Diploma in Manufacturing and Assembly

title: Caddie
tasks: Carrying the golfer’s club bag for the duration of the game and handing the golfer the required or requested club.
Cleaning the clubs and balls during the course of the game.
Knowing and advising the golfer of the distances (yardages) between the ball and the flag (pin).
Knowing where all the hazards are along the course and the best approach to avoiding these hazards.
Raking the bunkers and sand-traps after the golfer has used them.
Replacing divots (chunks of grass) if the golfer has cut them.
Holding the flag (pin) on the green while the golfer is putting.
Offering assistance or giving advice if asked.
Knowing the rules and keeping up-to-date with relevant golfing and golf course related information.

title: Cafe Worker
tasks: Preparing and serving food and beverages for consumption on the premises.
Taking customers' food and beverage orders.
Operating cash registers, accepting payments and preparing sales invoices.
Cleaning and setting tables for prospective customers.
Clearing away used dishes and cutlery from tables when customers are finished.
Washing dishes, cutlery and cooking utensils.
Cleaning cafe equipment such as coffee grinders, espresso machines and ice makers.
Participating in stocktakes and assisting in putting away new stock.
Providing backup to other cafe employees
entry_requirements: Learnership - Food and Beverage Services NQF Level 4
Further Education and Training Certificate in Food and Beverage Service (NQF Level 4)
Certificate in Food and Beverage Service (NQF Level 3)
Diploma in Food and Beverage Service

title: Confectionary Baker
tasks: Coordinating the forming, loading, baking, unloading, de-panning and cooling of batches of bread, rolls, pastry and confectionary products.
Checking the quality of raw materials to ensure that standards and specifications are met.
Measuring and weighing flour and other ingredients to prepare batters, doughs, fillings, and icings, using scales and graduated containers.
Monitoring oven temperatures and product appearance to determine baking times.
Adapting the quantity of ingredients to match the amount of items to be baked.
Observing colour of products being baked, and adjusting oven temperatures, humidity, and conveyor speeds accordingly.
Checking equipment to ensure that it meets health and safety regulations and perform maintenance or cleaning, as necessary.
entry_requirements: Learnership – Bread and Flour Confectionery Baking Level 2

title: Call or Contact Centre Manager

Developing and supervising a team of representatives, conducting performance evaluations and writing performance reports.
Identifying requirements which includes targets, specific data, and anticipated outcomes.
Managing the overall performance analysis of existing lists and programs.
Developing new lead targeting schemes and scripting for the optimization of existing programs.
Promoting sales culture that encourages and ensures staff satisfaction.

Learnership - Contact Centre Management NQF Level 5
Bachelor of Technology in Contact Centre Management
Postgraduate Diploma in Brand Contact Centre Management

tasks: Working from scripts and lists of contacts to promote goods and services by telephone in order to persuade potential customers to purchase products or services or to make donations to charitable causes.
Obtaining customer information such as name, address and payment method, and entering orders or commitments into computers.
Creating interest in goods and services, and seeking a sale or an agreement by the potential customer to meet with a sales representatives.
Arranging appointments for sales representatives to meet with potential customers.
Arranging the processing and despatch of purchased goods and services, information kits and brochures to customers.
Maintaining statistics of calls made and successes achieved and submitting periodic reports on telemarketing activities and results.
entry_requirements: Learnership - Contact Centre and BPO Support Level 3
Learnership - Contact Centre Operations NQF Level 4

title: Camera Operator (Film, Television or Video)
tasks: Discussing with director the types of film and  video techniques to be used, as well as focus and distance settings and camera angles.
Following directives from Director during filming over headset.
Moving cameras and adjusting controls to follow action scenes being photographed / filmed.
Selecting and setting up relevant equipment and accessories.
Checking  lighting has been set up as required.
Viewing scenes through viewfinder, making final adjustments and photographing / filming scenes.
Monitoring equipment during filming operation.
Moving cameras and adjusting controls to follow action scenes being photographed / filmed.
entry_requirements: Learnership - Further Education and Training Certificate: Film, Television and Video Production Operations Level 4
Further Education and Training Certificate in Film and Television Production
Certificate in Film and Television Production
Diploma in Film and Television Production

Adjusting and repairing masts, supporting structures, clearance lights, control panels, control cabling and wiring, and other electrical and mechanical devices.
Repairing and setting optical instruments such as microscopes, telescopes, theodolities, sextants.
Checking whether assembled units conform to specifications and ensuring stipulated performance and sensitivity by standard tests.
Calibrating precision instruments using standard weights and measures, jigs and fixtures, and hand tools to adjust and align parts and small balancing weights.
Testing circuits in electronic timepieces.
Programming of computers or electronic instruments, such as numerically controlled machine tools.
Maintaining industrial machines, applying knowledge of mechanics, shop mathematics, metal properties, layout, and machining procedures.

tasks: Advising on the facilities available and promoting publicity in relation to events, shows and activities.

Controlling the selection, supervision and performance of staff.
Ensuring compliance with health and safety regulations.
Ensuring that facilities are kept clean and in good condition.
Establishing and managing budgets, controlling expenditure and ensuring the efficient use of resources.
Planning and directing daily operations.
Planning and organising the range and mix of entertainment, attractions, cultural activities, and sports and fitness programmes to be offered by the park.

title: Faculty Head
tasks: Controlling administrative operations such as budget planning, report preparation, expenditure on supplies, equipment and services.
Controlling selection, training and supervision of staff.
Determining educational programs based on frameworks established by education authorities and governing bodies.
Developing and enforcing a disciplinary code to create a safe and conducive environment for students and teachers.
Directing administrative and clerical activities concerning student admissions and educational services.
Evaluating the work of teachers and lecturers by visiting classrooms, observing teaching methods, reviewing instructional objectives and examining learning materials.
Implementing systems and procedures to monitor school performance and student enrolments.
Organising and implementing methods of raising additional funds in conjunction with parent and community groups and sponsors.
Promoting the educational program, and representing the service or institution in the wider community.
Providing leadership and guidance to teaching, academic and administrative staff as well as to students.

title: Specialist Physician (General Medicine)

Undertaking laboratory tests and diagnostic procedures.
Prescribing therapeutic treatment and procedures.
Treating by medication rather than surgery.

title: Cane Furniture Maker
tasks: Designing cane furniture.
Examining furniture to determine the best method for repair or restoration.
Soaking rolls of cane in warm water.
Stretching cane over frameworks.
Crisscrossing cane strands to form a thick woven article.
Gluing and tacking the cane ends.
Recommending finishes and furniture styles, using knowledge of products, fashions and styles.
Mixing finishing ingredients to obtain desired colours or shades.
Painting and staining cane furniture.

title: Reinforced Plastics and Composite Trades Worker

Encasing uncoated wire, cord, cable and optic fibre in plastic.
Examining outputs for defects and conformity to specifications.
Recycling waste plastic materials.
Making artificial eyes and contact lens discs, making and repairing spectacle frames and plastic parts of orthopaedic appliances.

title: ICT Systems Analyst
tasks: Consulting with users to formulate and document requirements and with management to ensure agreement on systems principles.
Coordinating and linking the computer systems within an organisation to increase compatibility.
Developing functional specifications for use by systems developers.
Expanding or modifying systems to improve work flow or serve new purposes.
Identifying and analysing business processes, procedures and work practices.
Identifying and evaluating inefficiencies and recommending optimal business practices, and system functionality and behaviours.
Taking responsibility for deploying functional solutions, such as creating, adopting and implementing system test plans.

Bachelor of Technology in Information Technology

title: Car Compactor Operator
tasks: Driving portable car crushers/compactors to car junkyards, positioning them and setting them up.
Loading cars onto the crushing bed by operating lifting claws or magnets that are built into car crushers/compactors.
Operating crushers/compactors that crush cars as flat as possible in order to reduce their size and facilitate storage and transport to recycle plants.
Keeping records of all crushing/compacting operations.

title: Cardiologist
tasks: Prescribing medication and recommending special diets and exercise to a patient.
Performing corrective surgery where necessary.
Working in conjunction with other specialists (especially Anaesthetists) during surgery.
Conducting coronary bypass surgery.
Removing fatty deposits from closed or inflamed blood vessels.
On rare occasions transplanting a heart from a donor into a patient’s chest cavity.
entry_requirements: NCS Bachelor pass with Maths and Science

title: Sonographer
tasks: Operating or overseeing operation of radiologic, ultrasound and magnetic imaging equipment to produce images of the body for diagnostic purposes.
Explaining procedures, observing and positioning patients, and using protection devices to ensure safety and comfort during examination, scan, or treatment.
Position imaging or treatment equipment, monitoring video displays, and adjusting settings and controls according to technical specifications.
Reviewing and evaluating developed x-rays, video tape, or computer generated information to determine if images are satisfactory for diagnostic purposes and recording results of procedures.
Monitoring patients' conditions and reactions, reporting abnormal signs to a medical practitioner.
Measuring and recording radiation dosage or radiopharmaceuticals received and used for patients, following prescription issued by a medical practitioner.
Administering, detecting and mapping radiopharmaceuticals or radiation in patients' bodies, using radioisotope, camera or other equipment for diagnosing and treating diseases.
entry_requirements: National Senior Certificate - Diploma Entrance or National Certificate (Vocational)
National Senior Certificate - Degree Entrance or National Certificate (Vocational)

title: Surgeon
tasks: Examining each patient thoroughly, reviewing the medical history and consulting with other Doctors to be sure an operation is necessary.
Explaining to the patient and his or her family about what a surgical operation entails.
Treating injury, deformity, and disease by manual and instrumental means.
Removing or replacing a diseased organ or tissue.
Checking the equipment, instruments and surgical setup to be sure everything needed for an operation is present and sterile.

title: Personal Care Assistant
tasks: Helping persons who are disabled or chronically ill with their activities of daily living.
Assisting clients with personal, physical mobility and therapeutic care needs.
Helping with daily activities, such as helping the individual bathe, eat, prepare meals and maintain their home.
Providing clients with compassionate, considerate assistance with their hygiene, exercise, medication and communication.
Providing rehabilitative assistance for individuals who have had surgery or been ill.
Helping exercise the client by walking with him or her or helping with arm and leg stretches if the person is confined to bed or in a wheelchair.
Accompanying clients to social events such as games or crafts sessions.

title: Career Development Practitioner
tasks: Studying and analysing jobs performed in an establishment by various means, including interviews with workers, supervisors and management, and writing detailed position, job or occupation descriptions from information obtained.
Preparing occupational information or working on occupational classification systems.

Advising and working on the foregoing and other aspects of job and occupation analyses in such fields as personnel administration, workforce research and planning, training, or occupational information and vocational guidance.
Studying and advising individuals on employment opportunities, career choices and further education or training that may be desirable.
entry_requirements: National Examination of the Professional Board for Psychology (Counsellor)

title: Caretaker / cleaner
tasks: Cleaning building floors, walls, windows, restrooms, fixtures and furniture by dusting, sweeping, mopping, scrubbing, vacuuming or polishing using specific equipment and procedures.
Mixing water and detergents or acids in containers and preparing cleaning solutions according to specifications.
Servicing and restocking restrooms.
Gathering and emptying refuse bins and moving refuse to refuse collection area.
Setting up, arranging or removing decorations, tables, chairs, ladders or scaffolding to prepare facilities for events such as banquets or meetings.
Monitoring building security and safety by locking doors after operating hours and checking electrical appliance use to avoid hazardous situations.
Mowing and trimming lawns and shrubbery using mowers and hand and power trimmers.
Clearing debris and refuse from grounds.
Making adjustments or minor repairs to heating, cooling, ventilating, plumbing or electrical systems.
Notifying managers concerning the need for major repairs or additions to building operating systems.
entry_requirements: Learnership - Specialist Hygiene and Cleaning Level 2

title: Clearing and Forwarding Agent
tasks: Carrying out customs clearing procedures for exports or imports.
Checking import/export documentation to determine cargo contents, and classifying goods into different fee or tariff groups, using a tariff coding system.
Ensuring that export/import licenses and other formalities are in order.
Ensuring that insurance is in order.
Signing and issuing bills of lading.
entry_requirements: Further Education and Training Certificate NQF Level 3 or Grade 11
Learnership - Freight Forwarding and Customs Compliance (Generic) Level 3
Learnership - Freight Forwarding and Customs Compliance (Finance and Purchasing) Level 4

title: Carpet Cleaner
tasks: Inspecting carpets to identify the correct cleaning method required.
Selecting and applying cleaning agents to remove stains from carpets and upholstery.
Calculating correct solution strength for shampoos and cleaning chemicals.
Filling carpet cleaning machines with correctly mixed cleaning solutions.
Cleaning carpets and upholstered furniture using cleaning machines and their attachments.
Inspecting the cleaned carpet after drying to ensure cleanliness.
Applying stain-repellent chemicals to the carpet and upholstery to help maintain its cleanliness.
Pushing pile-lifting machines over carpets and brushing pile to raise and fluff it up.
entry_requirements: Learnership - Specialist Hygiene and Cleaning Level 2

title: Industrial Designer
tasks: Detailing and documenting the selected design for production.
Determining the objectives and constraints of the design brief by consulting with clients and stakeholders.
Formulating design concepts for clothing, textiles, industrial, commercial and consumer products, and jewellery.
Harmonising aesthetic considerations with technical, functional, ecological and production requirements.
Negotiating design solutions with clients, management, and sales and manufacturing staff.
Preparing and commissioning prototypes and samples.
Preparing sketches, diagrams, illustrations, plans, samples and models to communicate design concepts.
Selecting, specifying and recommending functional and aesthetic materials, production methods and finishes for manufacture.
Supervising the preparation of patterns, programs and tooling, and the manufacturing process.
entry_requirements: National Diploma in Design and Technology
Bachelor of Technology in Design and Technology
NCS Bachelor pass with Maths and Science

title: Mechanical Fitter
tasks: Operating powered machines that may be manually or computer controlled.
Erecting machinery and equipment on site.

Inspecting machinery regularly and making any adjustments or repairs needed by removing any worn or damaged parts to install replacements, by sending a damaged part to the machine shop for repair or by doing the repair work themselves.
Marking the shape and dimensions of a part to be machined by studying blueprints and using measuring instruments.
Assembling and fitting machined parts, using drill holes and tap threads, if necessary, for bolting parts together.
Checking tightness of joints and operation of moving parts, and filing or chiselling parts to make final adjustments if the fit is not perfect.
Cutting, threading, bending and installing hydraulic and pneumatic pipes and lines.

title: Cartographer
tasks: Designing maps, graphics, illustrations and layouts.
Using computers to compile and produce graphs for specialist and general users.
Researching, selecting and evaluating map source data for use in the preparation or revision of maps and charts to various scales.
Analysing and evaluating “mappable” information.
Liaising with surveyors and designers regarding projects.
Collating data provided by remote sensing techniques (the means by which spatial and environmental data about the earth are acquired by sensors located in satellites and aircraft).
Operating a photogrammetric plotting instrument or a digital photogrammetric workstation (DPW), which views the photographs stereoscopically or in a 3D format.
Designing and maintaining geographical information (GI) databases.
Using desktop publishing packages to edit and formulate information.
Generalising map data to allow for a reduction in scale (derived mapping).
Checking and appraising the content and accuracy of maps, charts and printing proofs.
entry_requirements: National Senior Certificate - Diploma Entrance or National Certificate (Vocational) with Mathematics
Bachelor of Technology in Cartography & Surveying
Designation: Professional Geographical Information Science (GISc) Practitioner

title: Dispatching and Receiving Clerk / Officer
tasks: Identifying items and containers of incoming and outgoing shipments and verifying them against consignment records.
Ensuring outgoing shipments are in good condition and meet specifications.
Organising the external dispatch and internal distribution of goods with completed documentation.
Maintaining prescribed records of goods received and dispatched.

Placing prices or descriptive signs on backdrops, fixtures, merchandise or floor.
